title: SQL, JDBC, and transactions — Java Practice
description: Independent practice: Persist expenses in a relational database. Seven questions with explanations.
author: DailyCoder

questions.explanation: SQL NULL uses three-valued logic and dedicated predicates.

questions.prompt: Can a ? parameter normally stand for an arbitrary table identifier?

options.text: Only if the name contains no spaces

questions.explanation: Value parameters are not SQL identifier substitution.

questions.prompt: What should happen after a failure halfway through a manual transaction?

options.text: Commit the successful half by default

questions.prompt: What tradeoff does an index commonly introduce?

options.text: Faster targeted reads with extra storage and write work

questions.explanation: Indexes must be chosen for actual access patterns.

questions.prompt: What protects uniqueness against concurrent database writers?
questions.explanation: The database must enforce the invariant atomically.

questions.prompt: What should happen to a borrowed pooled connection after use?

options.text: Close it promptly to return it to the pool
Keep it forever in a static field

questions.explanation: Pool-aware close releases the lease for other callers.
The SQL structure is fixed; the amount placeholder is a value parameter. Parameter 1 becomes 1000. Only Food qualifies; resources close in reverse order.
